model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Recorded identity is this evaluating session's ACTUAL runtime model, Opus 5 (1M context), exact id claude-opus-5[1m], per #1058. The evaluator pinned in the agent definition frontmatter was not copied into these fields.
model.rule_conformance_note: The launching agent quoted two rules verbatim (#1077). (1) Element 8 sub-element 4 APPLICABILITY: applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields, NOT gated on a referenced code repository. My own agent definition DOES NOT MATCH: it gates sub-elements 3 AND 4 together on 'external_resources references a code repository, OR description/purposes identifies software production as a dataset output'. I applied the quoted rule. Immaterial to the outcome here: the code-repository condition is independently satisfied (external_resources names GitHub/Zenodo), so sub-element 4 is applicable under either reading. (2) Element 8 sub-element 4 THRESHOLD: my definition DOES NOT MATCH either. My definition says a publisher-only pointer (organisation root, project homepage) 'scores 0'; the quoted rule says such a pointer 'neither earns nor forfeits the point', and the quoted rule requires stating which of cases (a)-(c) applies on a 0. I applied the quoted rule and scored 0 under case (c), not because of any publisher-only pointer. (3) Element 4 per-sub-element applicability (#1060): my definition DOES MATCH the quoted rule and was applied as written.

issues_detected.description: Version numbering is internally out of order. The record gives version '2.0' for the June 2026 release, while version_access lists the two immediately preceding releases (October 2025, doi 10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, and June 2025, doi 10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) as Dataverse version 2.1. A later release carrying a lower Dataverse version number than its predecessors is not explained anywhere in the record, and no source_caveats block addresses it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a source_caveats note under version or version_access explaining that Dataverse versions are per-DOI and do not order across releases, or correct the version if the value was misread.

issues_detected.description: Temporal endpoint conflict left unreconciled. collection_timeframes states the funding award runs 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 per NIH RePORTER, and in the same entry states the dataset will continue to be updated through the end of the project in November 2026. The same November 2026 end date is repeated in updates.update_details. The award period and the stated project end differ by roughly three months with no comment.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note whether November 2026 reflects a no-cost extension or a source discrepancy, in the manner the record already uses for the 2025/2026 release-date conflict.

issues_detected.description: Mild tension between the de-identification claim and the donor detail carried in known_biases. is_deidentified asserts data cannot be matched to a human subject, while known_biases.affected_subsets records donor characteristics for both lines (a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma; a healthy male Northern European donor). These are published characteristics of catalogued cell lines rather than identifiers, so the claim holds, but the record does not say so.
issues_detected.recommendation: State explicitly that donor characteristics are published attributes of the ATCC and HipSci catalogue entries and are not identifiers of a traceable individual.

issues_detected.description: Distribution format is documented at the container level only. distribution_formats and every resource entry give format ZIP and media_type application/zip; no field states what data formats the archives contain (mzML, RAW, OME-TIFF, h5ad, TSV, FASTQ or otherwise), and no character encoding is given. A reuser cannot determine from this record what they would be reading after unzipping.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the internal data formats per archive alongside the ZIP container, and add encoding for any text-based components.

issues_detected.description: The processing chain that produced the distributed archives is unstated. preprocessing_strategies carries one entry that says only that perturb-seq is distributed as both a processed atlas and raw sequence data, inferred from archive naming, and its caveat records that the June 2026 listing carries no per-file processing description. No cleaning, labeling, annotation, imputation or QC step is described for any modality, and no software is named for the mass-spectrometry search, the image processing, or the construction of the CRISPRi cell atlas.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the per-modality processing pipelines and their software, or state explicitly for each modality that the release documentation does not disclose them.

issues_detected.description: The only processing software named in the record is disclaimed as absent from the release. external_resources names the Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline as the software used to integrate CM4AI input data streams, while preprocessing_strategies.source_caveats and known_limitations both state that the computed cell maps, which that integration produces, are explicitly not included in this release. What produced the ten archives actually distributed is therefore still unstated.
issues_detected.recommendation: Separate the map-building toolkit from the per-modality processing software that produced the archives in this release, and name the latter.

issues_detected.description: Software and external deposits are named without resolvable identifiers. The Cell Mapping Toolkit is described as released via GitHub with tools archived in Zenodo, but no repository URL, package name, release tag or Zenodo DOI is given. The five raw_sources entries name MassIVE deposits with no MassIVE accession numbers, and the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas is named as hosted on Figshare with no Figshare DOI.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the GitHub organisation and repository, the Zenodo DOI, the MSV accessions and the Figshare DOI.

issues_detected.description: Three immunofluorescence archives carry an issued date of 2026-07-15, later than the 2026-06-17 publication date of version 2.0 that the record assigns to the release. The record identifies this in source_caveats and in distribution_dates rather than leaving it silent, so it is disclosed rather than concealed, but no resolution is offered.
issues_detected.recommendation: State whether the three archives were added to version 2.0 after initial publication, which would explain the later file dates.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level or column-level metadata anywhere in the record. The variables slot is unused and is_tabular is absent, so nothing describes the fields inside the perturb-seq atlas, the SEC-MS elution profiles or the AP-MS interaction tables.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variable metadata for the tabular components, or state that per-file data dictionaries live inside the archives.

issues_detected.description: The embargo is documented without an end condition. confidential_elements records that the external perturb-seq links for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and MDA-MB-468 cells are marked embargoed, and known_limitations repeats it, but no expected release date or triggering publication is given.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the embargo end date or the publication event that lifts it, if the release record states one.

semantic_insights: The record is emphatically well grounded in its sources. Fifteen separate source_caveats blocks distinguish what the June 2026 release page states from what is carried over from the March, June and October 2025 pages, the project preprint and the project portal, and each inference is labelled as an inference.

Two source conflicts are resolved with a stated ranking rather than silently: the portal's 'Released on: June 17, 2025' against the Dataverse publication date of 2026-06-17, resolved in favour of the Dataverse record as the higher-ranked source; and the portal's 523 imaged proteins against the October 2025 page's 464, where neither figure is asserted for this release.

The file inventory is arithmetically self-consistent. total_file_count of 10 matches the six file_collections summing to 10 (2+3+2+1+1+1), and distribution_dates splitting 7 archives on 2026-06-17 and 3 on 2026-07-15 matches the per-resource issued dates exactly.

The DOI prefix 10.18130 is correctly used for University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), and every related release DOI shares that prefix. Preprint DOIs use 10.1101 (bioRxiv), which is correct for the cited works.
Cell lines are identified by Cellosaurus RRIDs (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J), the correct RRID namespace for cell lines rather than the SCR_/AB_ forms the rubric names.

Both NIH grant numbers parse against NIH conventions: 1OT2OD032742-01 (activity code OT2, institute OD) and 5U54HG012513-02 (U54, NHGRI), with the RePORTER core project number and a supplement serial recorded in the notes.

The ethics posture is coherent for a cell-line dataset. human_subject_research false, is_deidentified with a stated basis, sensitive_elements_present false with a substantiated reason, and no consent or participant-privacy blocks fabricated to fill the schema.

Person identity resolution is handled carefully rather than assumed. Each of the three governance and ethics contacts is matched to an author ORCID with the matching basis stated, and the Ravitsky entry explicitly flags that the stated affiliation and the email domain disagree.
instances use B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs consistently across all five modality entries, giving machine-readable topic typing rather than prose alone.

Cross-block licensing is consistent: data_use_permission no_commercial_use, the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms spelled out in full, and ip_restrictions requiring separate commercial license negotiation all agree.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Format matches 10.XXXX/... and the 10.18130 prefix is University of Virginia Dataverse, which agrees with the landing page host and the citation's stated repository. Cell-line RRIDs (CVCL_0419, CVCL_B5P3) add secondary identifiers for the source material.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description ~1,100 characters covering modalities, cell lines, treatment arms, distribution route and interim status
sub_elements.quality_note: Description names all four modalities, both cell lines with their perturbation conditions, the ten-archive distribution through UVA Dataverse, and closes by stating what the release does not contain (computed cell maps, embargoed components). Substantially above the 200-character bar and specific throughout.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 31 entries including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, CRISPR/Cas9, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, paclitaxel, vorinostat, subcellular imaging, Bridge2AI
sub_elements.quality_note: Well beyond the 5-keyword bar. Covers assay modality, cell line, compound, disease area, technique acronym and expansion, and the program, so both acronym and full-form searches resolve.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; six file_collections each with nested resources carrying id, name, format, media_type, file_type and md5
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page is a well-formed Dataverse persistent-identifier URL. The hierarchical structure is genuine: collections grouped by modality, each with file_count and named archive resources, all ten reachable and checksummed.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of, target_dataset doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM; version_access.versions_available lists five releases with DOIs
sub_elements.quality_note: The relationship to the immediately preceding release is typed and carries a DOI target plus a note on what this release adds. The release lineage back to May 2024 is enumerated with per-release DOIs.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 conditions; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions: commercial use requires separate license negotiation with UCSD, Stanford and/or UCSF; copyright held by the Regents of the University of California except raw spatial-proteomics image data (Stanford)
sub_elements.quality_note: Access policy is stated as operative terms, not a license label: attribution, share-alike, no additional technological restrictions, and citation of both the data and the related publication. IP restrictions name the specific copyright holders per data package, with a caveat recording that the commercial-licensing text is drawn from the preprint and earlier release pages.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance: 'Human Subjects: No' and 'FDA Regulated: No'; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present true, temporary pre-publication embargo on the KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq external links; sensitive_elements_present false; data_governance notes all ten archives listed with public file access
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated regulatory_restrictions and confidentiality_level slots are unused, but the substance is present and specific in adjacent access-layer fields: regulatory status affirmatively determined, a real confidentiality constraint (component embargo) recorded with which components it covers, and the access level of the ten distributed archives stated. Scored on content rather than slot placement.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: Dataverse persistentId URL; distribution_formats.notes: 'The dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP; individual files below the 1.9 GB web download limit may be selected from the files table, and the Dataverse Data Access API provides programmatic access.'
sub_elements.quality_note: No per-file download_url is given, but the sub-element admits platform access instructions in place of direct links, and these are concrete and actionable: the resolvable landing page, the file-selection route, the 1.9 GB web limit that forces it, and the API alternative for the multi-gigabyte image archives.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format ZIP, media_type application/zip; each of the ten resources carries format, media_type, compression, file_type (data_file or metadata_file) and md5
sub_elements.quality_note: Container format, MIME type and per-file typing are complete and consistent across all ten archives, with MD5 checksums published for integrity verification. Scored 1 for what this sub-element asks (formats and file types specified); the deeper problem that only the container is described is charged against Element 3 sub-element 2, where standardisation for reuse is the question.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: one typed entry with DOI; external_resources: five entries covering the CM4AI preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), the project portal https://cm4ai.org/, the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas on Figshare, the Cell Mapping Toolkit, and FAIRSCAPE https://fairscape.github.io; third_party_sharing records MassIVE deposits
sub_elements.quality_note: Both required categories populated with substantive entries, each carrying a note explaining its relation to the release. The Figshare and MassIVE pointers lack accessions, which is charged as a correctness issue rather than an absence.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET. distribution_formats is populated, page resolves to a Dataverse record whose ten archives are listed with public file access, and the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license explicitly permits sharing and adaptation. Sub-elements 1-4 are therefore applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with ten ZIP archives; page resolves to the UVA Dataverse record; license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 permits share and adapt
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out share, adapt, attribute, link the license, indicate changes, no commercial use, share-alike, no additional restrictions
sub_elements.quality_note: A named standard license with its permissions and obligations written out, plus the attribution and citation expectation. A reuser can determine what they may do without consulting the license text.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.evidence: format: ZIP; media_type: application/zip on every resource; compression: zip; no encoding field anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the container is documented. ZIP with application/zip is a correctly typed standard, but it tells a reuser nothing about what the archives hold: no mzML, RAW, OME-TIFF, FASTQ, h5ad, TSV or equivalent is named for any of the four modalities, and no character encoding is given for text components. The record's own source_caveats confirm the June 2026 listing carries no per-file descriptions, so the omission is inherited from the source, but the sub-element measures whether formats are standardized for integration and this record does not support that determination.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels: the packaging standard (RO-Crate, enumerated), the framework that produced it (FAIRSCAPE), and this record's own schema and class. Instance typing against Bridge2AI substrate and topic vocabularies adds ontology grounding for the modalities.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.evidence: variables: slot absent from the record
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable-level metadata of any kind. The instances entries type the measurement kinds with CURIEs, which is instance-level rather than variable-level, and nothing describes the columns of the perturb-seq atlas, the SEC-MS elution profiles or the AP-MS interaction tables.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four use_category entries (AI-ready functional-genomics research, AI model training, cellular process analysis, analysis of architectural changes under disease, treatment or perturbation); prohibited_uses: 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; existing_uses cites the iPSC perturbation atlas preprint
sub_elements.quality_note: Both directions covered. The prohibition is specific and reasoned rather than boilerplate, and it aligns correctly with the non-clinical, cell-line character of the data asserted in sensitive_elements. discouraged_uses is unused, which is a minor gap only.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Applied per sub-element per #1060, and the launching agent's quoted restatement of that rule matches my own agent definition. HUMAN-SUBJECTS CONDITION: NOT MET. Established from fields outside Element 4. E1 description names MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells, never participants or patients; E1 keywords are cell-line, assay and compound terms with no clinical or participant term; E8 collection_mechanisms describe AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, SEC-MS, confocal immunofluorescence and 10x Genomics CRISPRi screens, which are instruments rather than recruitment; and E8 direct_collection states is_direct false with 'Data were not collected from individuals. All measurements were made on established human cell lines obtained from third-party repositories'. This is positive evidence that the condition fails, not merely empty Element 4 fields, so the anti-circular rule does not resurrect it. GOVERNANCE CONDITION: MET. Element 2 access-layer fields state constraints that actually apply, not a record that none applies: confidential_elements records a temporary pre-publication embargo on two named components, ip_restrictions requires separate commercial license negotiation with named copyright holders, and license_and_use_terms sets data_use_permission no_commercial_use. Per #1060 the governance condition opens sub-elements 1-2 only and does not reach sub-elements 3-5.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Governance condition met via E2 fields: confidential_elements records an operative pre-publication embargo on the KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq components; ip_restrictions requires separate commercial license negotiation with UCSD, Stanford and/or UCSF; license_and_use_terms sets no_commercial_use. Human-subjects condition not met (see element applicability note). Determination rests on E1, E2 and E8 fields, not on Element 4's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153, Simon Fraser University), each 'per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record'; data_governance.committee_name: Data Governance Committee, committee_contact Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, UC San Diego); human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance: 'Human Subjects: No' and 'FDA Regulated: No'
sub_elements.quality_note: The sub-element's Look-for list names governance committee contacts explicitly, and the record supplies a named committee with a contact plus two named ethical review contacts, each resolved to an ORCID with the matching basis stated and disagreements flagged. The regulatory determination is recorded affirmatively rather than left blank. No data protection impact assessment is present, which is appropriate for non-clinical cell-line material. What is missing is any account of a review process or its outcome, which costs nothing here but is charged at Element 9 sub-element 5.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance condition as sub-element 1, evidenced from E2 access-layer fields. Human-subjects condition not met.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; deidentification_details: 'The release record answers "De-identified Samples: Yes". The project preprint states that CM4AI data are non-clinical, from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.'; known_biases: 'commercially available de-identified human cell lines'
sub_elements.quality_note: No named technique such as Safe Harbor, Expert Determination or k-anonymity appears, and none could: the material is catalogued cell lines supplied de-identified by ATCC and HipSci, so no de-identification procedure was performed by this project. The record states the de-identification status, gives the basis for it (non-clinical tissue culture, unmatchable to a subject with current knowledge), and attributes that basis to both the release record and the preprint. Demanding a technique that cannot exist for this data type would measure subject matter rather than documentation, so scored on the substantiated claim. Flagged as a low-severity note that known_biases carries donor characteristics alongside this claim without saying they are published catalogue attributes.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met and it is the only condition that opens this sub-element (#1060). E1 description and keywords name cell lines, assays and compounds with no participant, patient or clinical-research term; E8 collection_mechanisms describe instruments rather than recruitment; E8 direct_collection.is_direct is false with 'Data were not collected from individuals'. The governance structures present (Data Governance Committee, component embargo, commercial-licensing restriction) are not a participant signal and do not reach this sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants exist to protect; participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk are absent, correctly so
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. There are no participants whose privacy could be protected or whose re-identification risk could be assessed, so scoring 0 would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met and it is the only condition that opens this sub-element (#1060). Same E1, E8 evidence as sub-element 3; the governance condition does not reach it.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent absent; direct_collection.is_direct false, 'Data were not collected from individuals'
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Consent is obtained from participants and this dataset has none; the source material is commercially catalogued cell lines whose original donor consent sits with ATCC and HipSci, not with this release.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met and it is the only condition that opens this sub-element (#1060). Same E1, E8 evidence as sub-element 3; the governance condition does not reach it.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation absent; no participants were recruited
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. No population was enrolled, so there is no at-risk group to protect and no one to compensate.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), triple negative breast cancer line from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female, available from ATCC; KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3), iPSC from a healthy male Northern European donor, available from HipSci via MTA; sampling_strategies: targeted selection of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes implicated in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders; description names treatment arms (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat) and differentiation states (undifferentiated iPSC, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte)
sub_elements.quality_note: The subpopulations slot is unused, but the population analogue for a cell-line dataset is characterised thoroughly: both lines identified by RRID with donor origin and disease context, their provenance repositories and access route, the treatment and differentiation arms that partition the release, and the selection criteria for the interrogated gene set. This is the substance the sub-element asks for.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10; per-collection file_count 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1; per-archive sizes (4.6 GB, 3.8 GB, 4.2 GB, 171.8 KB, 93.9 KB, 113.3 KB, 135.8 KB, 30.2 KB, 73.3 KB, 1.1 MB) and MD5s; sampling_strategies: 11,739 targeted genes for the KOLF2.1J atlas, 200 genes perturb-seq and 523 proteins imaged for the TNBC dataset; notes: project holdings of 1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins and 21.4 TB
sub_elements.quality_note: The distributed inventory is counted exactly at the file level with sizes and checksums. Deeper instance counts are given with explicit caveats that the gene and protein figures come from the portal and from earlier releases rather than from this release's own listing, and that the portal's 523 conflicts with October 2025's 464. The record declines to assert per-release instance counts it cannot source, and says so, which is the honest handling of a gap in the source rather than an omission in the documentation.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: variables absent; is_tabular absent
sub_elements.quality_note: Neither field is present. Several components are inherently tabular (the SEC-MS elution profiles, the AP-MS interaction measurements, the perturb-seq atlas) and nothing describes their columns or flags them as tabular.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances: five entries, each with instance_type prose plus data_substrate and data_topic CURIEs (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/B2AI_TOPIC:19 immunofluorescence localization; :59/:28 SEC-MS elution profiles; :58/:26 AP-MS interactions; :64/:34 single-cell CRISPRi profiles; :63/:34 raw sequence reads)
sub_elements.quality_note: Every measurement type in the release is enumerated with both a readable description naming the cell line and treatment condition, and machine-readable substrate and topic terms. Disease and perturbation context (triple-negative breast cancer, paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPRi) is carried in the instance_type text.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies: two entries with is_sample and is_random flags, the targeted 200-gene selection and the genome-scale 11,739-gene CRISPRi coverage, each with a source_caveats block stating what is and is not asserted for this release; known_limitations: incomplete overlap of the protein sets interrogated by SEC-MS, IF imaging and perturb-seq, and unsuitability for integrated cross-modality analysis
sub_elements.quality_note: sampling_strategies is the sub-element's own named field and it is populated with unusual care, including the record's reasoning for setting is_sample false on the genome-scale component and an explicit statement that no source says so in terms. The incomplete-overlap limitation is a real structural quality issue for anyone attempting integration. anomalies and missing_data_documentation are unused, which is charged at Element 9 sub-element 3 rather than twice.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET (distribution_formats populated, Dataverse landing page with public file access, reuse-permitting license). All five sub-elements applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; issued: '2026-06-17T00:00:00Z'
sub_elements.quality_note: A version number, a maturity status and a publication date are all present. Flagged separately as a medium consistency issue that this 2.0 is numerically below the 2.1 recorded for the two preceding releases, unexplained.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; versions_available lists June 2026 (HIGT4C, v2.0), October 2025 (K7TGEM, v2.1), June 2025 (F3TD5R, v2.1), March 2025 (B35XWX, v1.4) and May 2024; version_details explains that each quarterly release is deposited under its own DOI and separately versioned within Dataverse
sub_elements.quality_note: A reuser can retrieve any prior release: each carries its own resolvable DOI, and version_details explains the two-level scheme (per-release DOI plus Dataverse internal version) that would otherwise confuse the numbering.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets.notes: 'The June 2026 release adds AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, which the October 2025 release did not include'; source_caveats: the description block ends with a trailing (2025-06-30) stamp identical to the June 2025 and October 2025 releases, indicating description text carried forward between releases; file_collections source_caveats: the June 2026 IF archives carry different MD5 checksums from the October 2025 archives of the same names
sub_elements.quality_note: A specific, verifiable inter-version change is stated (AP-MS added), and two documentation defects inherited from the source are recorded: description text carried forward unchanged between releases, and same-named archives whose contents differ by checksum. That last is exactly the kind of change a reuser needs flagged. No errata list as such, and the errata slot is unused, so the credit rests on genuine change documentation rather than on a formal changelog.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: Quarterly; update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'; retention_limit: long term preservation in the UVA Dataverse supported by committed institutional funds
sub_elements.quality_note: Both cadence and horizon are stated, corroborated from two sources (the release record and the project portal), and paired with a preservation commitment for after the update period ends. The November 2026 horizon sits three months past the stated award end, flagged as a low-severity consistency issue.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: both cell lines with RRIDs, donor origin and access route (ATCC; HipSci via MTA); raw_sources: five entries naming MassIVE deposits for SEC-MS and AP-MS raw data and the in-release raw SRA archive; acquisition_methods: a was_inferred_derived entry stating the KOLF2.1J atlas is a processed product of the paired raw archive; conforms_to: RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs produced using FAIRSCAPE
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance is traced in both directions: back to the source cell lines with catalogue identifiers, and out to the external repositories holding the corresponding raw data. The derivation relationship between the perturb-seq atlas and its raw archive is stated with its inferential basis labelled. was_derived_from and release_notes are unused, but RO-Crate provenance graphs are declared as the machine-readable carrier.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: three responses covering machine-readable hierarchical cell-architecture maps as AI-ready data from 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes, ethical AI-ready datasets to enable transformative biomedical AI, and mapping spatiotemporal cell architecture toward interpretable genotype-phenotype learning; addressing_gaps: two responses on the black-box problem in genomics ML and on the absence of AI-Ready properties in existing biomedical datasets
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose is stated at three levels of abstraction and paired with an explicit account of the gaps being filled, including a definition of what AI-Ready means to this project (FAIR, known provenance, characterized, machine-readable provenance graphs, explainable, ethically obtained). Specific and non-boilerplate throughout.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: 'Interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, in which predictions are traced to multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than produced by an opaque model' and 'Development of "visible" machine learning systems, including visible neural networks built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture'
sub_elements.quality_note: Two named ML task formulations, each specific enough to indicate what a model built on this data would do and what its architecture would rest on. They align coherently with the addressing_gaps account of black-box prediction.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: grantor National Institutes of Health with two grants, and grantor University of Virginia with the Frederick Thomas Fund; notes identify the awards as the Bridge2AI Functional Genomics award and the Bridge2AI Bridge Center award
sub_elements.quality_note: Both federal and institutional funders named, with the mechanism identified for each NIH award (OT2 Functional Genomics data generation, U54 Bridge Center) rather than the agency alone. The principal investigator is named from NIH RePORTER.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: grant_number: 1OT2OD032742-01, with notes recording the RePORTER core project number OT2OD032742, application 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2 for FY2025, award amount 5,289,382 and project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31; grant_number: 5U54HG012513-02
sub_elements.quality_note: Both NIH numbers parse correctly against the [application type][activity code][institute][serial]-[suffix] convention: OT2 with OD for the Office of the Director, and U54 with HG for NHGRI, which is the right institute for a Bridge2AI Bridge Center award. The supplement serial and award period are corroborated from RePORTER. The third entry is a named fund with no number, and the record says so explicitly rather than fabricating an identifier.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: 46 entries, 40 carrying ORCID identifiers, each with an institutional affiliation; citation lists the full author line; maintainers names the CM4AI Program Manager (Swathi Thaker, UAB, snthaker@uab.edu) and website support (Zhandos Sembay, UAB); data_collectors attributes modalities to UCSF, Stanford, UCSD and UVA with roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is unusually complete: named creators with persistent identifiers and affiliations, contributing institutions with their specific modality roles, named maintainers with contact addresses, and funding acknowledgements. One creator entry carries a source_caveats note where the release record's affiliation differs from other sources.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
elements.applicability_note: Sub-elements 1-2: data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) AND datasets shared (condition met above) - both applicable. Sub-element 3: software condition MET via E10 field external_resources, which references a code repository ('Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline software, released under a BSD-3 open source license via GitHub, with production-ready tools archived in Zenodo') and the FAIRSCAPE framework at https://fairscape.github.io - applicable. Sub-element 4: applied per the launching agent's verbatim rule (#1079), which makes it applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields (acquisition_methods and preprocessing_strategies are populated) and NOT gated on a referenced code repository. My own agent definition does not match, gating sub-elements 3 and 4 together on the repository condition; immaterial here because that condition is independently met. Sub-element 5: shared condition met - applicable.

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors, collection_timeframes all populated) and datasets shared
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: four entries - AP-MS on endogenously tagged cell lines; SEC-MS for proteome-wide complex and interaction mapping; immunofluorescence staining and confocal microscopy (ICC-IF) using Human Protein Atlas antibodies with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols established for MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2; single-cell CRISPRi screens using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit with a lentiviral CRISPR library and inducible dCas9 lines. data_collectors: UCSF, Stanford, UCSD and UVA with per-institution roles. collection_timeframes: creation and deposit 2025-02-27, award period, continued updates to November 2026
sub_elements.quality_note: All four modalities described at the level of the actual experimental setup, including the antibody resource, the automated sample-preparation protocols, the specific kit and the dCas9 induction system. Production sites are attributed to modalities with a caveat that the June 2026 listing gives locations collectively and the attribution comes from the preprint and earlier release pages. collection_timeframes honestly states that no explicit collection start and end dates are given.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: a primary-measurement entry (was_directly_observed true, was_reported_by_subjects false) naming AP-MS, SEC-MS, immunofluorescence confocal microscopy and single-cell CRISPR perturbation screens, and a derived-processing entry (was_inferred_derived true) on the KOLF2.1J atlas with its inferential basis stated; raw_data_sources: both cell lines with RRIDs and repositories; raw_sources: five raw deposits identified by modality, cell line and treatment
sub_elements.quality_note: Acquisition is typed with the schema's observation flags rather than described in prose alone, and the direct-versus-derived distinction is drawn explicitly with the derived claim labelled as an inference from paired archive names. Instrument specificity stops at the platform level (10x Genomics 3'HT, confocal microscopy) with no mass spectrometer models or software versions, which is a real limit but leaves the acquisition route understandable.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software condition met via E10 external_resources, which references a code repository (Cell Mapping Toolkit released via GitHub with tools archived in Zenodo) and the FAIRSCAPE framework with its documentation URL. Determination made from E10's field, not from Element 8's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: a single entry stating only that 'Perturb-seq data are distributed both as a processed CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas and as the underlying raw sequence data, in separate archives', with source_caveats 'Inferred from archive naming in the June 2026 file listing; that listing carries no per-file processing description'; cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols all absent
sub_elements.quality_note: The one preprocessing statement is an inference from filenames that a processing step occurred, not a description of what it did. Nothing describes mass-spectrometry search or quantification, image segmentation or quality control, read alignment or guide assignment, cell filtering, normalisation, labeling or annotation quality for any of the four modalities. The record is candid that the source listing carries no per-file processing description, which is the right disclosure, but the sub-element asks whether processing can be understood or replicated and from this record it cannot.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Applied per the quoted rule (#1079): applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields. acquisition_methods records a derived-processing step and preprocessing_strategies records that a processed cell atlas is distributed, so the data were processed. The repository condition is also independently satisfied via E10 external_resources, so the sub-element is applicable under my own definition's narrower gate as well.
sub_elements.evidence: software_and_tools: slot absent. machine_annotation_tools: absent. preprocessing_strategies: names no software in any field, including its prose. external_resources (the only tooling-bearing slot populated): 'Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline software, released under a BSD-3 open source license via GitHub, with production-ready tools archived in Zenodo', notes 'Software used to integrate CM4AI input data streams'; and 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, https://fairscape.github.io', notes 'Framework used to package CM4AI data, software, metadata and provenance graphs'. conforms_to: RO-Crate packaging 'produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'
sub_elements.quality_note: Slot carrying the evidence: external_resources. Scoring 0 under case (c) of the quoted threshold, with case (a) also holding. Case (c): the record names a pipeline and then says that pipeline's outputs are not in this release. The Cell Mapping Toolkit is described as the software that integrates CM4AI input data streams, and integration produces the computed cell maps, which preprocessing_strategies.source_caveats and known_limitations both state are explicitly not included in this release. So the one processing pipeline named is the one whose product is absent. Case (a) covers the remainder: no software is named for the mass-spectrometry search, the confocal image processing, or the construction of the distributed CRISPRi cell atlas, which the record itself identifies as a processed product. FAIRSCAPE does not carry the point either, falling under case (b): it is named as the packaging and metadata-provenance framework that produced the RO-Crate wrappers and the release metadata archive, not as software that processed the data being distributed. A reader of this record cannot tell what produced the ten archives. Note that no publisher-only pointer decided this outcome; per the quoted rule such a pointer neither earns nor forfeits the point.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: five entries including the CM4AI preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, full author list), the project portal https://cm4ai.org/, the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas on Figshare, the Cell Mapping Toolkit, and FAIRSCAPE https://fairscape.github.io with its MIT license; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; existing_uses cites the iPSC perturbation atlas preprint with PMCID PMC11580897 and doi 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards (RO-Crate, enumerated), frameworks (FAIRSCAPE, with license), the methods publication and a downstream analysis publication are all referenced, each with a note explaining its relation to the release. Two publications carry resolvable DOIs and one a PMCID.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries - scope_limitation (interim release, not in completed final form); coverage_limitation (no predicted cell maps); coverage_limitation (KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq under temporary pre-publication embargo); integration_limitation (SEC-MS, IF and perturb-seq interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets); integration_limitation (most suitable for single-modality bioinformatics rather than integrated cross-modality analysis); methodological_limitation (meaningful analysis requires domain expertise)
sub_elements.quality_note: Six limitations, each assigned a category from the schema's enum and each stating a consequence a reuser would act on. The integration limitations are the most valuable: they tell a user attempting multimodal analysis, which is the dataset's headline purpose, that this release will not support it well and why.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: bias_type representation_bias; bias_description 'Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'; affected_subsets names both lines with donor characteristics (a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma; a healthy male Northern European donor)
sub_elements.quality_note: Typed against the BiasTypeEnum vocabulary rather than described in loose prose, and the affected_subsets field does the work that matters: it names the two donors whose genetic backgrounds the entire release rests on, which is the concrete form representation bias takes in a two-cell-line dataset. Only one bias category is recorded and future_use_impacts is unused, so downstream social impact is not anticipated, but the one entry present is correctly categorised and substantive.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: slot absent. The discrepancies that are documented are all in source_caveats and concern the documentation rather than the data: conflicting release dates (portal 2025 versus Dataverse 2026), conflicting protein counts (portal 523 versus October 2025 page 464), description text carried forward between releases, IF archives dated after the version publication date, and differing MD5 checksums for same-named archives across releases
sub_elements.quality_note: No anomaly in the data itself is documented anywhere: no outliers, batch effects, failed runs, low-quality images, dropout characteristics or excluded samples. The record's discrepancy reporting is genuinely good but it is metadata-source reconciliation, not dataset quality assessment, and the sub-element asks for the latter.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false, with sensitivity_details 'The release record states that the dataset does not involve human subjects, that samples are de-identified, and that the data are not FDA regulated. The project preprint states that CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures.'; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present true, naming the two embargoed perturb-seq components; prohibited_uses warns against clinical decision-making or patient care without regulatory oversight
sub_elements.quality_note: The negative determination on sensitivity is affirmative and substantiated from two sources rather than left blank, and it is paired with a positive determination on confidentiality that names exactly which components are constrained. The prohibited_uses warning about clinical use is the one content warning a non-clinical laboratory dataset actually needs. content_warnings is unused, appropriately for this material.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries whose review_details read identically, 'Named ethical review contact for the release, per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record', each followed by contact_person and a source_caveats block on identity matching. No conflicts of interest disclosure anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: What is present is contact information, not review details. Neither entry describes a review that took place, its scope, its determination or its date, and the identical review_details text in both entries is a label rather than a finding. No conflict of interest statement appears for any of the 46 creators, the ethics contacts or the Data Governance Committee, despite the record noting the preprint's plan for a Data Access Committee to supervise potential dual licensing for commercial use, which is precisely a context where conflicts would be disclosed. The contacts themselves were credited at Element 4 sub-element 1, where the sub-element explicitly asks for governance committee contacts, so this is not double-penalised.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared: CONDITION MET. Publication identified: CONDITION MET - citation is populated, external_resources carries the CM4AI preprint with doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, and existing_uses cites a bioRxiv publication with PMCID PMC11580897. All five sub-elements applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; citation names 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; maintainers: 'Long term preservation is provided by the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), supported by committed institutional funds'; distribution_formats.notes names the Dataverse Data Access API; DOI prefix 10.18130 is UVA's
sub_elements.quality_note: The publisher slot itself is unused, but the hosting platform is established four times over from independent fields and is internally consistent with the DOI prefix. Dataverse is a recognised research repository and the record documents its preservation commitment and its programmatic access route, not merely its name.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified (citation populated; external_resources carries the CM4AI preprint DOI; existing_uses cites a publication with PMCID) and datasets shared
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full 46-author list, year 2026, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license_and_use_terms requires that publications referencing the data cite both the related publication and the data collection itself
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, ready-to-use citation in repository format with authors, year, title, resolver URL, repository and version, matching the doi field exactly. The license terms additionally state the dual-citation expectation, so a user knows to cite the methods preprint alongside the data.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: RO-Crate is a recognised community packaging standard and it is declared both in prose and as an enumerated value, alongside the record's own schema and class. B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs on the instances entries add community vocabulary conformance at the content level.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: CM4AI project portal https://cm4ai.org/ described as 'providing documentation, data release listings, tools and publications for CM4AI'; FAIRSCAPE https://fairscape.github.io; the methods preprint; page resolves to the Dataverse record; maintainers names website support contacts at UAB
sub_elements.quality_note: Two resolvable documentation sites plus the landing page and the methods preprint, each annotated with what it provides. No webinars or tutorials are listed, but the project portal is identified as the documentation hub and named support contacts are given for website questions.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of, target_dataset doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, with a note identifying it as the October 2025 release and stating that June 2026 adds AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 cells; version_access.versions_available carries DOIs for three further prior releases; third_party_sharing records the MassIVE and Figshare deposits
sub_elements.quality_note: The relationship is typed with a schema enum value, points at a resolvable DOI, and is explained. Only one related dataset is expressed in the typed slot, but the full release lineage is available with DOIs through version_access and the external raw-data deposits through third_party_sharing, so cross-referencing is not obstructed.

strengths: Source discipline is the record's defining quality. Fifteen source_caveats blocks separate what the June 2026 release page states from what is carried over from the preprint, the project portal and the March, June and October 2025 release pages, and every inference is labelled as one, including the reasoning behind setting is_sample to false on the genome-scale CRISPRi component.

Two source conflicts are resolved with a stated ranking rather than silently absorbed: the portal's 2025 release date against the Dataverse 2026-06-17 publication date, and the portal's 523 imaged proteins against the October 2025 page's 464, where neither figure is asserted for this release.

The distributed inventory is complete and internally consistent: ten archives with names, sizes, MD5 checksums, per-file publication dates and file typing, organised into six modality collections whose file counts sum exactly to the stated total, with distribution_dates matching the per-resource dates.

Attribution and identifiers are unusually thorough: 46 creators with 40 ORCIDs and affiliations, cell lines identified by Cellosaurus RRID with donor origin and access route, two NIH grant numbers that parse correctly with the RePORTER core project and award period, and each governance contact resolved to an author ORCID with the matching basis stated and disagreements flagged.

Limitations are honest about what the release cannot do: six typed entries including the incomplete overlap of protein sets across modalities and the statement that the release suits single-modality analysis rather than the integrated cross-modality analysis that is the project's headline purpose.
weaknesses: The processing chain that produced the ten archives is unstated. preprocessing_strategies contains one entry inferring from filenames that processing occurred, and no cleaning, labeling, annotation, imputation or quality-control step is described for any of the four modalities.

No software is documented for what is actually distributed. The software_and_tools and machine_annotation_tools slots are unused, and the one processing pipeline named in external_resources, the Cell Mapping Toolkit, produces the computed cell maps that the record states are explicitly not in this release.

Distribution is documented at the container level only. Every file is ZIP with media_type application/zip, and no field states what data formats the archives hold or what character encoding text components use, so a reuser cannot plan an integration.

No variable-level metadata anywhere: the variables slot is unused and is_tabular is absent, leaving the columns of the perturb-seq atlas, the SEC-MS elution profiles and the AP-MS interaction tables undescribed.

No dataset-level quality assessment. The anomalies slot is unused and nothing records outliers, batch effects, failed runs, excluded samples or dropout characteristics; the discrepancies that are documented concern the release documentation rather than the data.

Ethical review is reduced to contact details. Both ethical_reviews entries carry identical placeholder review_details naming a contact, with no review scope, determination or date, and no conflict of interest disclosure appears anywhere despite the record noting a planned Data Access Committee overseeing potential commercial dual licensing.
Version numbering is internally out of order and unexplained: this release is version 2.0 while the two releases preceding it are recorded as Dataverse version 2.1.
recommendations: Name the per-modality processing software that produced the distributed archives, with versions, distinguishing it from the Cell Mapping Toolkit whose cell-map outputs are excluded from this release: the mass-spectrometry search and quantification tools, the confocal image processing pipeline, and the alignment, guide-assignment and atlas-construction software behind cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip.
Record the data formats inside each ZIP alongside the container, and give encoding for text components, so a reuser knows whether they are receiving mzML, RAW, OME-TIFF, FASTQ, h5ad or tabular files.
Populate variables for the tabular components, or state explicitly that per-file data dictionaries ship inside the archives, and set is_tabular accordingly.

Add an anomalies entry covering dataset-level quality: excluded samples, failed acquisitions, batch structure across the treatment arms, and any known image or spectrum quality issues, or state that the release documentation discloses none.

Replace the placeholder review_details in both ethical_reviews entries with the scope, determination and date of the review each contact oversaw, and add a conflicts of interest statement, particularly in view of the planned Data Access Committee role in commercial dual licensing.
Explain the version numbering in a source_caveats note under version or version_access, since 2.0 for June 2026 sits below the 2.1 recorded for the October 2025 and June 2025 releases.

Supply resolvable identifiers for the resources currently named only by host: the GitHub organisation and repository plus the Zenodo DOI for the Cell Mapping Toolkit, the MSV accessions for the five MassIVE deposits, and the Figshare DOI for the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas.

Reconcile the November 2026 project end stated in updates and collection_timeframes with the 2026-08-31 award end recorded from NIH RePORTER, and record the embargo end date or the publication event that lifts it.
